title: The Nightly Resort Charge for a Household That Skis and Eats on the Mountain
content:
The nightly resort charge of a Resort Lodging stay turns on what else the household holds with the collective, because the shuttle, the fitness centre and the pools the charge pays for are already paid for elsewhere by a household that skis and eats on the mountain all season. Two kinds of record are read for the season of the stay: the household's season passes under the Season Pass Programme, and its dining plans under Mountain Dining Plans, each read for its standing and the season it is held for.

Where a season pass stands active for the season of the stay on the household account and a dining plan stands active for that season as well, the member share of the unit type's nightly resort charge is taken, being 70 percent of it.

Where one of those two stands active for that season but not the other, the part member share of that nightly charge is taken, being 85 percent of it.

Where neither stands active for that season, the unit type's nightly resort charge is taken in full.

| Season pass standing active for the season | Dining plan standing active for the season | The nightly charge taken |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | 70 percent of the unit type's nightly resort charge |
| yes | no | 85 percent of it |
| no | yes | 85 percent of it |
| no | no | the whole of it |

### Three hypothetical households, on a unit type whose nightly resort charge is taken here as 40.00 USD

A household holding a season pass standing active for the season of the stay and a dining plan standing active for that same season is charged 28.00 USD a night, being 70 percent of 40.00 USD.

A household holding the season pass but no dining plan standing active for that season is charged 34.00 USD a night, being 85 percent of 40.00 USD; a household holding the dining plan but no season pass standing active for that season is charged the same.

A household holding neither for that season is charged the whole 40.00 USD a night.
